rootCause.wrongValueObserved: activateManualSubscription with billingPeriodDays 365: "PROBE create.cycle = undefined update.cycle = undefined create.periodEnd-periodStart days = 365". rollCycles on that row (cycle MONTHLY by schema default, externalPayment true, 2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01): "PROBE select = {"tenantId":true,"cycle":true,"periodEnd":true} rolled periodStart = 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z periodEnd = 2026-02-01T00:00:00.000Z", when it should be 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.
rootCause.note:
I reproduced the bug on the current tree with a throwaway Jest probe. It lives only in the scratchpad (scratchpad/rc863/probe.spec.ts) and I ran it with `--roots` pointed there. No repo files were changed.

The named cause is correct on both halves:
1. **Activation never sets `cycle`.** Both branches of the `tenantSubscription.upsert` call in apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.ts (about lines 963-995) leave out `cycle`. I called the real `activateManualSubscription` with `billingPeriodDays: 365` and stubbed dependencies, then captured the upsert arguments: `create.cycle` and `update.cycle` were both `undefined`, and `periodEnd` minus `periodStart` was 365 days. The column defaults to MONTHLY (platform.prisma:47, `cycle BillingCycle @default(MONTHLY)`). So a prepaid annual row is stored as MONTHLY on create and keeps whatever cycle it already had on update.
2. **The cron rolls by `cycle` only.** `rollCycles` in apps/api/src/billing/billing-cron.service.ts (about lines 484-498) selects only `{tenantId, cycle, periodEnd}`. It never reads `periodStart` or `externalPayment`, and it calls `addCycle(start, s.cycle)`, which adds 1 month unless the cycle is ANNUAL. Run on the real service, a 365-day external row (2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01) rolled to periodEnd 2026-02-01, one month instead of a year. That is exactly the wrong value test-plan T3 predicts.

The brief's own check doesn't work. `jest -t "REG-ROLL-MANUAL-ANNUAL"` can't be "green today" because no test by that name exists: grep for MANUAL-ANNUAL and manual-annual under apps/api/src returned nothing. The repro-test task has to write it as REG-B863-ROLL (per the test plan) rather than flip an existing test.

In the probe, `activateManualSubscription` threw after the upsert because my stub had no `findMany`. That doesn't affect the upsert arguments I captured, since they were recorded before the throw. I did not run the probe for 90- or 180-day periods; by the same code path they would also roll +1 month, but that is inferred, not observed.

I reproduced the bug on the current tree and the brief's named cause is what produces the wrong value. The source tree was not changed: git status shows only the pre-existing pipeline and doc changes.

**How I reproduced it:** I copied `apps/api/src/platform-admin/platform-admin.service.spec.ts` into the session scratchpad at `rc864/rc864.spec.ts` and rewrote its relative imports as absolute ones. I then added one probe test inside the "B557 books a compensating delta" describe block and ran it with a temporary Jest config (`rc864/jest.json`) using the repo's own ts-jest. The probe test and the neighbouring B557 test both passed as tests; the wrong value is in the probe's printed output.

**What the probe does:**
- Step 1: a TRIAL, PRODUCTION tenant with planKey SCALE and basePriceSnapshot null calls `updateTenantPriceOverride({monthly:1200})`.
- Result: the snapshot is back-filled to 1200 and PLAN_CHANGED is emitted with amountDelta 1200, even though the tenant is on TRIAL. That is the gate at `platform-admin.service.ts:1439-1440`, which reads no status or class and never calls `isPayingRow`, followed by the unconditional emit at :1455-1462.
- Step 2: `activateManualSubscription` runs on the same tenant, which now has snapshot 1200.
- Result: it sees wasPaying=false and isPaying=true, prices the contribution at 1200, and emits a second +1200 (lines 1001-1037). The ledger totals 2400 while the run-rate is 1200. Before the fix the expected result is a single +1200, at activation only.

**Caveats:**
- The mocks do not keep state between calls. I fed step 2 the post-override row by hand, `{status:TRIAL, subscription:{planKey:SCALE, basePriceSnapshot:1200, discount:0}}`, matching the upsert I saw in step 1.
- I did not run `reconcilePriceLedger` (BillingService is mocked in this suite). The claim that it does nothing here is from reading the code only: `billing.service.ts` around lines 522-523 returns early when the old monthly equals the new one (1200 = 1200).
- The brief's probe tag `REG-OVERRIDE-BACKFILL-TRIAL` does not exist yet; grep found nothing in `apps/api/src`. The existing test at spec lines 1144-1165 asserts `amountDelta:1200` without any tenant status, so it will have to change with the fix.

Used 11 of the 12 allowed tool calls.

I reproduced the bug on the current tree. I wrote a scratch jest spec in the session scratchpad, ran it with `--roots <scratch> --roots <rootDir>` from apps/api, and deleted it afterwards. It fed MrrService.computeOverview two subscription rows: STARTER at base 59 with no discount, and BUSINESS at base 349 with a discount of 10. It had no add-ons. The output shows top-level baseMrr = 408, which is gross (349 + 59). BUSINESS in byPlan shows baseMrr = 339, which is net (349 - 10). The byPlan rows add up to 398. The gap between 408 and 398 is exactly the 10 discount.

This matches the cause the brief names. In apps/api/src/billing/mrr.service.ts, line 242 has `baseMrr += base;` and never subtracts the discount. Line 249, in the same loop, has `row.baseMrr = roundMoney(row.baseMrr + base - discount);`. Both lines read the same `base` and `discount` values from lines 235-236. No other term makes up the difference.

The existing tests in apps/api/src/billing/mrr.service.spec.ts still pass on this tree: "computes MRR = ..." expects baseMrr 408 and "breaks MRR down by plan" expects BUSINESS 339. The run shows 2 passed and 12 skipped. Together they lock in the inconsistency this bug describes.

Two things I did not do. A first attempt to run the probe with ts-node failed because `@routeflow/pricing/dist` is not built in this worktree, so I switched to jest, which has the moduleNameMapper. I also did not revert line 249 to test the cause by mutation. I tied the gap to that line by arithmetic only: 408 - 398 = 10, the only discount in the fixture. The repo has no changes from me. The git status is the same as the pre-existing snapshot.
